# QS-CFW-6476-89 - Quality specification - bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (52100)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-6476-89

Scope
- This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (52100) manufactured at Plant P2. It applies to forgings and finished rings produced to drawing CFW-6476-89 and to all incoming raw forgings that will be processed and finished under this specification.
- Background and intent: the bearing ring is intended for use in high-cycle radial applications. The requirements reflect material and geometric controls necessary to ensure service life and interchangeability. The controls emphasize hardness, bore geometry, and mass limitations to manage forging integrity and subsequent heat treat response.

Requirements table
- The table below captures the mandatory acceptance criteria. Values in the table are measured as produced and after heat treatment where indicated.

| Characteristic | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Material designation | 52100 per part drawing CFW-6476-89 |
| Hardness (post heat treat) | The hardness range for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is 29-32 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance (final machined) | The bore diameter tolerance for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is ±0.04 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight (as forged) | The maximum forging weight for bearing ring CFW-6476-89 (CFW-6476-89) is 119.0 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of forging laps, cold shuts, and subsurface discontinuities that would impair machining or final part performance. |

Inspection method
- Receiving inspection
  - Inspect incoming forgings for conformance to the maximum forging weight requirement by recording the forging mass from the shipping documentation and verifying mass against the forging. If doubt exists, confirm mass on calibrated weighing equipment and record results in the inspection record.
  - Visually inspect for gross forging defects that would prevent machining or heat treatment. Document any findings on the incoming inspection form.
- Dimensional inspection
  - Bore diameter: verify final machined bore conforms to the bore diameter tolerance by measuring at multiple axial locations using a calibrated bore gauge or internal micrometer. Measurements must be taken after final machining and before any press-fit operations or heat treatment that could alter the bore. Record the measured bore diameters and note deviations from nominal within the inspection record.
  - Rationale: multiple axial measurements detect taper and localized out-of-round conditions that a single measurement would not capture, reducing risk of assembly issues.
- Hardness verification
  - Hardness shall be measured on the finished bearing ring after final heat treatment and stable temper. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester set to the appropriate scale for HRC. Perform a minimum of three indents in the bearing race area on representative rings across a production run to confirm uniform hardness within the specified range. Ensure indent locations avoid machined surfaces and include areas representative of service loading.
  - Rationale: confirming hardness post heat treat ensures proper transformation and temper; the specified range controls wear resistance and toughness balance for 52100.
- Weight confirmation
  - Verify the forging mass does not exceed the maximum forging weight by reviewing forging records and mass documentation provided by the forging supplier. If forging mass equals or exceeds the maximum forging weight, initiate the nonconformance process.
  - Rationale: controlling forging mass limits flash, nonmetallic inclusion distribution, and material flow during forging, which can affect final microstructure and dimensional accuracy.
- Sample and frequency guidance
  - Inspection frequency and representative sampling shall follow plant inspection practice and known process capability. For routine production, periodic verification of hardness and dimensional stability must be maintained and documented to demonstrate control.
- Measurement equipment and calibration
  - All measurement devices used for verifying the listed requirements must be in a current calibration status traceable to the plant calibration system. Calibration certificates and the equipment identification shall be recorded in the inspection record.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any part or forging found outside the requirements table shall be identified, segregated from conforming material, and labeled with a nonconformance tag. The tag shall reference this specification and include a brief description of the nonconformance.
- Evaluation and disposition
  - The responsible quality engineer shall evaluate nonconforming items to determine acceptability for use, rework, or scrap based on root cause and impact to performance. Where hardness is out of range, disposition may include reheat and controlled temper only if metallurgical analysis supports restoration to the specified hardness range. Where bore diameter exceeds tolerance, rework by machining back to draw-on dimensions may be considered only if sufficient material remains and functional geometry can be met without violating drawing limits.
  - Examples of disposition rationale:
    - A ring with hardness below the specified range may indicate under-hardening; reheat followed by a controlled quench and temper may restore properties if microstructure analysis confirms absence of tempering-induced defects.
    - A ring with bore out of tolerance due to machining error may be reworked if final geometry and surface integrity can be restored; otherwise scrap is required.
- Documentation and approval
  - All disposals, rework steps, and final dispositions must be documented on the nonconformance report and approved by the quality engineer. Records must include the nature of the nonconformance, measurements, root cause analysis, corrective actions, authorization for rework or use-as-is, and final disposition.
- Records to keep
  - Maintain the following records in the document control system:
    - Incoming inspection records and forging mass documentation.
    - Final dimensional inspection reports including bore measurements and instrument identification.
    - Hardness test records including tester identification, readings, and locations of indents.
    - Calibration certificates for measuring equipment used.
    - Nonconformance reports with dispositions and approvals.
    - Process change or corrective action records tied to recurrence prevention.
  - Retain records in accordance with plant retention policy and make available for audits and customer review upon request.

Notes
- This specification is authoritative for the listed part at Plant P2. Any deviations or concessions require written approval from quality engineering and operations management.
